audit.title: Architecture (DTA Technical Standard)

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong section leads — "DTA Request Management serves as the central hub for discovery and requests" is liftable. The page intro opens with a principle ("separation of concerns") rather than defining what the DTA architecture *is*; a one-sentence canonical definition would improve the top chunk.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Good — 6 headings, 0 level skips, sensible H2/H3/H4 nesting, bulleted responsibilities. Weak spot: no comparison table contrasting the two contracts, which is the single most extractable structure for this content.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak — measured 0 numerals, 0 units. Mentions "rate limits and time zones" and role-based permissions with zero concrete values, network names, or version identifiers.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Weak — only 1 internal link (llms.txt). "Chainlink CCIP" and "NAVLink feed" are named but not linked to their canonical concept pages.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Moderate — component roles are crisply stated, but "DTA," "Transfer Agent," and "NAVLink" lack a self-contained one-line definition near first use.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak — 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, no og/twitter tags. Head metadata could not be verified from the served content; CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a full read.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Not applicable to a pure concept page; no code expected. Scored neutral, not penalized.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Moderate — answers "what are the components" well, but no "how do I," no troubleshooting, no symptom-phrased headings. No coverage of when to choose local vs cross-chain beyond the mechanism.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Good, consistent naming. Two blemishes: literal "(Image: Image)" placeholder and the odd parenthesized "(DTA Request Management) and (DTA Request Settlement)".

audit.summary: This is a clean, well-structured conceptual page explaining the two-contract DTA architecture (Request Management vs Request Settlement) and their local/cross-chain interaction. Its biggest strength is clear separation-of-concerns prose with sensible section chunking; its biggest weakness is a near-total absence of extractable specifics, authoritative inline links, and machine-readable metadata — the page states rules exist ("rate limits and time zones") but never quantifies them, and carries no JSON-LD, canonical URL, or dates. Honest verdict: solid explanatory writing sitting below its retrieval potential because it gives engines almost nothing quantitative or linkable to cite.

recommendations.title: Add a canonical two-contract comparison table
recommendations.where: under "## Core components", before the H4 subsections
recommendations.issue: contract roles are split across prose bullets; 0 tables measured
recommendations.change: add a table with columns *Contract | Owner/Deployer | Multi-tenant? | Core responsibilities | Token authority* for Request Management vs Request Settlement
recommendations.why: tables let engines extract the distinguishing *reasons* and answer "what's the difference between DTA Request Management and Settlement" in one lift.

recommendations.title: Link canonical references inline
recommendations.issue: "uses Chainlink CCIP" and "using the NAVLink feed" are unlinked
recommendations.change: link "Chainlink CCIP" to its docs concept page and "NAVLink feed" to its definition page on first mention
recommendations.why: inline links to primary/canonical sources raise credibility and citation rate, and help entity resolution.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/question-phrased headings
recommendations.issue: headings are concept-titled ("Interaction patterns") not query-shaped
recommendations.change: add H3s like "How does DTA settle across chains?" and "When is settlement local vs cross-chain?" leading with a one-sentence answer
recommendations.why: devs/agents query by question; question-titled sections win retrieval that concept titles lose.

recommendations.title: Quantify the operational rules
recommendations.issue: "operational rules (such as rate limits and time zones)" — no values
recommendations.change: state actual limits/units (e.g., request cap per window, supported settlement windows, supported chains/CCIP lanes) or link to the page that defines them
recommendations.why: quantitative specifics are among the highest-lift changes for citation; qualitative-only prose underperforms.

recommendations.title: Add a lead-in canonical definition
recommendations.issue: opens with a design principle, not a definition of the architecture
recommendations.change: prepend one liftable sentence: "The DTA technical standard splits onchain transfer-agency into two contracts: a public, multi-tenant Request Management contract and a private, single-tenant Request Settlement contract."
recommendations.why: a crisp self-contained opener is the chunk engines lift for "what is the DTA architecture."

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD, canonical URL, and last-updated
recommendations.issue: 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no dates measured
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` schema with `headline`, `dateModified`, canonical URL, and `inLanguage`
recommendations.why: structured metadata and freshness signals improve agent trust and parseability (E-E-A-T).

recommendations.title: Fix presentation blemishes
recommendations.issue: literal "(Image: Image)" and "(DTA Request Management) and (DTA Request Settlement)"
recommendations.change: supply real alt text / caption for the diagram; remove the stray parentheses
recommendations.why: clean, unambiguous presentation is independently rewarded; a diagram with descriptive alt text adds extractable content.

antiPatterns: Placeholder artifact: literal "(Image: Image)" with no alt text — the architecture diagram contributes zero extractable content.
Vague qualifiers standing in for data: "rate limits and time zones" with no values.
Named-but-unlinked entities ("Chainlink CCIP", "NAVLink feed") — weakens attribution and entity resolution.
No keyword stuffing, no marketing fluff, no unresolved "see above" references — clean on those.
offPageNotes: JSON-LD, canonical URL, and og/twitter tags are almost certainly injected by the site template; verify against a full `<head>` capture before treating as a page-level defect.
The page already references `/llms.txt` — good site-level discoverability signal; ensure this page is listed there.
Freshness cadence (visible dateModified) is a site-template concern that would lift this and every sibling concept page.
